extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent practitioners, and patent owners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for determining patent term, eligibility for patent term adjustment (PTA) under 35 U.S.C. 154 and for patent term extension (PTE) under 35 U.S.C. 156, plus procedures, calculations, limits, and related duties (e.g., disclosure, confidentiality, multiple-application rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Twenty-year term for utility and plant patents
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after June 8, 1995 (other than design patents), patent term begins on issue date and ends 20 years from the filing date of the application in the United States or, if claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c), from the earliest such application's filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patents have different terms (see separate criterion). Continuations, divisionals, and continuation-in-part filings ending date rules follow the earliest benefit claim. Changes introduced by Patent Law Treaties Implementation Act added reference to 386(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patents have a term of fourteen years from grant for patents issued before May 13, 2015, and fifteen years from grant for design patents issued from applications filed on or after May 13, 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 35 U.S.C. 173 and MPEP § 1505; 'design patents' includes certain international design applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 385.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-June 8, 1995 patent term rule (17-years-or-twenty-year greater-of)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents that were in force on June 8, 1995, or issued from applications filed before that date have a term equal to the greater of the twenty-year-from-filing term or seventeen years from grant, subject to terminal disclaimers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimers may reduce term; changes to 35 U.S.C. 154 caused some printed terminal disclaimer dates to be incorrect and may be corrected via Certificate of Correction under 37 CFR 1.323.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing application and international application term rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent granted on a continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part filed on or after June 8, 1995 ends twenty years from the filing date of the earliest application for which benefit is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c). Patents from international applications that enter the U.S. national stage have terms ending twenty years from the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation-in-part claiming benefit under 365(c) of an international application ends twenty years from the parent international filing date when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority and provisional filings not counted in twenty-year term
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d), 365(a), 365(b), 386(a), or 386(b) and domestic priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) (U.S. provisional) are not considered in computing the twenty-year term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The twenty-year term is computed from the U.S. filing date (or earliest benefit U.S. filing date), not the foreign or provisional priority filing dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer effects on expiration date
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine the original expiration date for a patent subject to a terminal disclaimer, examine the terminal disclaimer language in file history; if it disclaims the terminal portion beyond an earlier patent's expiration, the earlier patent's expiration typically governs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If printed date on face is incorrect due to statutory changes, patentee may request a Certificate of Correction under 37 CFR 1.323. If terminal disclaimer specifies a specific date, that date controls. A PTE under 35 U.S.C. 156 may still be applied to patents subject to a terminal disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which applications are eligible for PTA/PTE (date-range eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility and applicable rules depend on application filing date: applications filed between June 8, 1995 and May 28, 2000 follow former 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and 37 CFR 1.701; applications filed on or after May 29, 2000 follow amended 35 U.S.C. 154(b) (Patent Term Guarantee Act / AIA amendments) and 37 CFR 1.702–1.705. Patents issuing from applications filed before June 8, 1995 are not eligible for term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully apply effective-date provisions: multiple CFR/section versions exist; examiners/personnel must determine which version applies to the specific application/patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for extension under former 35 U.S.C. 154(b) / 37 CFR 1.701 (June 8, 1995–May 28, 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be extended for delays due to (1) interference or derivation proceedings under 35 U.S.C. 135(a), (2) secrecy orders under 35 U.S.C. 181, and/or (3) appellate review by the Board or Federal courts reversing an adverse determination of patentability, provided the patent is not subject to a terminal disclaimer for related subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total extension is sum of non-overlapping delay periods up to a maximum of five years. Extensions for successful appeals are limited (e.g., ineligible if subject to terminal disclaimer). Periods reduced by time attributable to appellate review before 3 years from filing and by applicant lack of due diligence as determined by the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of delay periods under 37 CFR 1.701
rubrics_metrics.description: Delay periods are calculated as the sum of non-overlapping days for: (c)(1) interference/derivation proceedings involving the application (from institution to termination), (c)(2) secrecy order time (sealed condition, examiner’s answer under secrecy, notification periods), and (c)(3) appellate review time (from appeal filing to final decision in favor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overlap between delay categories should not be double-counted; the extension runs from the patent's expiration date. Specific measurement start/end points are provided for each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Term Adjustment guarantees under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and 37 CFR 1.702 (post-May 29, 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: PTA provides days added for Office delays including failure to: (A)(i) mail certain notifications or notice of allowance within 14 months, (ii)/(B) issue patent within 3 years (subject to exceptions), (A)(ii)/(iii)/(iv) respond/act/issue within specified 4-month windows after applicant reply/appeal/PTAB/federal decisions or after issue fee paid — generally, one day of adjustment per day of Office delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different subparagraphs cover (1) failure to take certain actions within time frames (14 months/4 months), (2) three-year pendency guarantee (with exclusions), and (3) adjustments for derivation/interference, secrecy orders, and successful appellate review. Regulations limit overlap and provide measurement rules; effective-date variations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement rules for 14-month notification and 3-year pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications granted on/after Jan 14, 2013, the 14-month measurement is from filing under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or national stage commencement under 371; older versions measure international applications based on when 371 requirements were fulfilled. The 3-year pendency is measured from the actual filing date under 111(a) or date national stage commenced under 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory changes (AIA and technical corrections) altered measurement dates; examiners must select correct regulatory version. See MPEP discussion of pre/post-2013 and other effective-date nuances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlap limitation on adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: When periods of delay attributable to multiple statutory grounds overlap, the total period of adjustment shall not exceed the actual number of days the issuance of the patent was delayed (no double-counting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute non-overlapping days only; regulations provide methods to ensure accurate counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of PTA for applicant delay / failure to engage reasonable efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: The adjustment period shall be reduced by the period during which the applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution; for responses to Office notices, any cumulative time in excess of three months taken to reply is deemed a failure for reduction purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director will prescribe regulations identifying circumstances that constitute failure to engage reasonable efforts. Applicant may show 'due care' to reinstate up to three additional months per response (see Director's reinstatement authority).

rubrics_metrics.name: Due care / reinstatement of reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall reinstate all or part of cumulative reduction periods if, prior to patent issuance, the applicant shows that despite all due care they were unable to respond within the 3-month period; reinstatement cannot exceed three additional months per response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must present convincing evidence of due care before issuance; reinstatement is limited by statute/regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for PTA determination and reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Director regulations, the Office will determine the period of patent term adjustment and transmit a notice of that determination no later than the date of patent issuance; the applicant is provided one opportunity to request reconsideration of the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant is dissatisfied after reconsideration, exclusive remedy is civil action against the Director in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia within 180 days of the Director’s decision. Chapter 7 of Title 5 (APA) applies to such actions. Determinations are not challengeable by third parties prior to grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and final-judgment effect on patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: A final judgment changing the period of adjustment shall be served on the Director, who will alter the patent term accordingly; the applicant's exclusive remedy from Director reconsideration is a civil action in EDVA within 180 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director will proceed to grant the patent after completion of the PTA determination even if applicant appeals the determination; timing and service requirements are set by statute/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners do not decide PTA or PTE eligibility (printing and corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners make no decisions regarding patent term extensions; any administrative delay-based PTA granted will be printed on the face of the patent in appropriate locations. If applicant disagrees with printed information, they may petition under 37 CFR 1.181 and may obtain a Certificate of Correction under 37 CFR 1.322 if petition granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term and extension information (filing date, continuing data, issue date, and extensions printed on patent) together determine expiration. Petition and Certificate of Correction procedures are available to correct printed errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTE under 35 U.S.C. 156 (regulatory review extension) — general availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent term extension under 35 U.S.C. 156 may be available for delays caused by premarket regulatory review (e.g., FDA) and is separate from and additive to any adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154; patents issuing from applications filed before June 8, 1995 may be eligible for PTE under 156 even if not eligible for PTA under 154.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2750 et seq. for detailed eligibility, application contents, filing dates, and calculation methodologies. PTE is contingent on regulatory review period calculations and regulatory-agency determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-application/one-patent-per-product rule for PTE (37 CFR 1.785)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one patent may be extended for a given regulatory review period for any product. If multiple extension applications are filed for the same patent, certificate issuance is based on the first-filed application; if multiple patents/applications are filed for the same regulatory review period, tie-breakers include earliest patent issue date or election by patent owner; priority may go to the marketing applicant (holder of regulatory approval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple applications exist, the Office may request identification of the holder of regulatory approval within a non-extendable period (usually one month). Failure to provide requested info may be treated as conclusive that applicant is not holder. Determinations under 1.785 are included in the final determination of eligibility under 1.750.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Extension issuance and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: When an extension is appropriate, after notice and one-month period for response, a Certificate of Extension (often initially issued under seal) is signed by the Director and mailed/delivered to the applicant with a copy to the regulatory agency; a notice is published in the Official Gazette and the certificate is placed in the patent file and patent electronic database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All original papers from the PTE application become part of the patent record; Certificates of Extension are handled similarly to Certificates of Correction or terminal disclaimers in the database; trade secret/confidential material handling rules apply (see below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade secret, confidential, and protective-order material handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials submitted in connection with a PTE application are generally part of the record and public unless properly identified and expunged; proprietary/trade secret info should be submitted in accordance with MPEP § 724.02 and identified by page/line/word as necessary. The Office will not initially determine which material is proprietary—applicant must identify it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information will not be made public as part of the patent file before a certificate of extension is issued. If the Office receives a FOIA request, applicant will be notified and given opportunity to substantiate proprietary claims before disclosure. If not expunged before certificate issuance, the information will be open to public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure in PTE proceedings (37 CFR 1.765 / MPEP § 2762)
rubrics_metrics.description: A duty of candor and good faith toward the USPTO and the Secretary of HHS or Agriculture rests on the patent owner, its agent, each attorney/agent representing the patent owner, and every other individual substantively involved in a PTE proceeding. Individuals aware of material adverse information not previously made of record must disclose it to the Office or the Secretary as soon as practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information is 'material' when there's a substantial likelihood the Office or Secretary would consider it important to determinations in the PTE proceeding. Disclosures must be accompanied by copies of written documents and filed with the appropriate entity; duplicate certified copies required if material to both Office and Secretary. Failure to disclose (fraud, bad faith, gross negligence) proven by clear and convincing evidence will result in ineligibility for extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of third-party participation in PTE proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: PTE proceedings before the Office are ex parte matters between the patent owner (or agent) and the Office; submissions by or on behalf of third parties (protests or otherwise) will not be considered and will be returned or otherwise disposed of without consideration, unless invited by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although public input to the regulatory agency determination is permitted (e.g., due diligence petitions), no analogous third-party participation is provided for Office proceedings under 35 U.S.C. 156; see In re Dubno and related MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express withdrawal of application for PTE (37 CFR 1.770)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for extension of patent term may be expressly withdrawn before a determination is made under § 1.750 by filing a duplicate written declaration of withdrawal signed by the owner of record or agent; withdrawal is effective when acknowledged in writing by the Office; no refund of filing fee is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application may not be expressly withdrawn after the date permitted for reply to the final determination. Requests for withdrawal after a determination must be submitted on or before the date permitted for reply and be accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with petition fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to identify proprietary/material and petition to expunge
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting proprietary or trade secret material in a PTE application, applicant should identify specific proprietary portions; if necessary, a petition to expunge must be filed before issuance of the certificate to prevent disclosure. If petition to expunge is not filed prior to certificate issuance, the material becomes public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will notify applicant if a FOIA request is received for such material and provide an opportunity to substantiate claims before disclosure. See MPEP § 724.02 and PTE-specific handling.
